13.

15. */
16. package metric
17. 
18. import (
19. 	"context"
20. 	"encoding/json"
21. 
22. 	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric"
23. 	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/instrument"
24. 	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit"
25. 	otelMetric "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric"
26. )
27. 
28. var _ Metric = (*Meter)(nil)
29. 
30. // Metric interface attempts to abstract high-level aspects of the observability features,
31. // this would make it much easier to swap the base sdk without having to change too
32. // many implementation details.
33. type Metric interface {
34. 	// Register gives a name to the metric and initializes the provider.
35. 	Register(name string)
36. 
37. 	// Dump is responsible to read the metrics and output all the gathered data.
38. 	Dump(ctx context.Context) (any, error)
39. 
40. 	// Close shutsdown the meter.
41. 	Close(ctx context.Context) error
42. }
43. 
44. // Meter is currently wrapping opentelemetry meter functionalities while adhering to
45. // the Metric interface functionality.
46. type Meter struct {
47. 	reader   otelMetric.Reader
48. 	provider *otelMetric.MeterProvider
49. 	meter    metric.Meter
50. }
51. 
52. // NewMeter returns a new meter.
53. func NewMeter() Meter {
54. 	return Meter{}
55. }
56. 
57. // Register gives a name to the metric and initializes the provider.
58. func (m *Meter) Register(name string) {
59. 	m.provider = m.newManualProvider()
60. 	m.meter = m.provider.Meter(name)
61. }
62. 
63. // Dump is responsible to read the metrics and output all the gathered data.
64. func (m *Meter) Dump(ctx context.Context) (any, error) {
65. 	return m.reader.Collect(ctx)
66. }
67. 
68. // Close shutsdown the meter.
69. func (m *Meter) Close(ctx context.Context) error {
70. 	return m.provider.Shutdown(ctx)
71. }
72. 
73. // GetSyncHistogram returns a new histogram with the given name and unit.
74. func (m *Meter) GetSyncHistogram(
75. 	name string,
76. 	unit unit.Unit,
77. ) (instrument.Int64Histogram, error) {
78. 	return m.meter.Int64Histogram(
79. 		name,
80. 		instrument.WithUnit(unit),
81. 	)
82. }
83. 
84. // GetSyncCounter returns a new counter with the given name and unit.
85. func (m *Meter) GetSyncCounter(
86. 	name string,
87. 	unit unit.Unit,
88. ) (instrument.Int64Counter, error) {
89. 	return m.meter.Int64Counter(
90. 		name,
91. 		instrument.WithUnit(unit),
92. 	)
93. }
94. 
95. // DumpScopeMetricsString returns a string representation of the metrics.
96. func (m *Meter) DumpScopeMetricsString(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
97. 	data, err := m.reader.Collect(ctx)
98. 	if err != nil {
99. 		return "", err
100. 	}
101. 	jsonBytes, err := json.MarshalIndent(data.ScopeMetrics, "", "  ")
102. 
103. 	if err != nil {
104. 		return "", err
105. 	}
106. 
107. 	return string(jsonBytes), nil
108. }
109. 
110. // Get returns the meter.
111. func (m *Meter) Get() metric.Meter {
112. 	return m.meter
113. }
114. 
115. func (m *Meter) newManualProvider() *otelMetric.MeterProvider {
116. 	// Register a manual reader.
117. 	m.reader = otelMetric.NewManualReader()
118. 	return otelMetric.NewMeterProvider(
119. 		otelMetric.WithReader(m.reader),
120. 	)
121. }

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"In **OpenTelemetry-Go** version **v1.16.0**, there was a *migration in how metric instrument units are handled*. This was due to changes introduced in the [OpenTelemetry Specification](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/3248), which clarified how units are associated with instruments.

Here's an overview of the **unit migration process** and what you need to change in your code if you are upgrading to v1.16.0 or later.

---

## **What changed in v1.16.0?**

1. **Unit as a field:**  
   The `unit` property is now an explicit, first-class argument in the instrument creation process.

2. **Unit is immutable:**  
   Once set on an instrument, the unit cannot be changed.

---

## **Migrating Your Code**

Previously, most Go OTEL metric instrument creation methods either did not take a `unit` or took it as an option. Now, you provide the unit *at creation*.

### **Before (v1.15.x and earlier):**
```go
meter := global.Meter("example")
counter, _ := meter.Int64Counter("requests_total")
```

### **After (v1.16.0+):**
```go
meter := global.Meter("example")
counter, _ := meter.Int64Counter(
    "requests_total",
    metric.WithUnit("requests"),
)
```
- `WithUnit` should be provided if your instrument has a unit (for dimensioned metrics like "seconds", "bytes", etc.).
- For dimensionless units, you can omit or specify an empty string.

### **For All Instruments:**
This applies to counters, histograms, gauges, etc.

---

## **Automated Migration Help**

- The breaking change might result in compile errors if unit-related options no longer match the API. Check your metrics instrument creation for obsolete parameters or missing units.
- If you have custom libraries, update their APIs to propagate units correctly.

---

## **Relevant PRs and Docs**
- [OpenTelemetry-Go release v1.16.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.16.0)
- [Metric API migration notes](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/4271)
- [OpenTelemetry Specification unit clarification](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/3248)

---

## **Summary Table**

| Old Style              | New Style (v1.16.0+)                  |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| meter.Int64Counter("x")| meter.Int64Counter("x", metric.WithUnit("unit")) |

---

This was due to changes introduced in the [OpenTelemetry Specification](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/3248), which clarified how units are associated with instruments.

Here's an overview of the **unit migration process** and what you need to change in your code if you are upgrading to v1.16.0 or later.

---

## **What changed in v1.16.0?**

1. **Unit as a field:**  
   The `unit` property is now an explicit, first-class argument in the instrument creation process.

2. **Unit is immutable:**  
   Once set on an instrument, the unit cannot be changed.

---

## **Migrating Your Code**

Previously, most Go OTEL metric instrument creation methods either did not take a `unit` or took it as an option. Now, you provide the unit *at creation*.

### **Before (v1.15.x and earlier):**
```go
meter := global.Meter("example")
counter, _ := meter.Int64Counter("requests_total")
```

### **After (v1.16.0+):**
```go
meter := global.Meter("example")
counter, _ := meter.Int64Counter(
    "requests_total",
    metric.WithUnit("requests"),
)
```
- `WithUnit` should be provided if your instrument has a unit (for dimensioned metrics like "seconds", "bytes", etc.).
- For dimensionless units, you can omit or specify an empty string.

### **For All Instruments:**
This applies to counters, histograms, gauges, etc.

---

## **Automated Migration Help**

- The breaking change might result in compile errors if unit-related options no longer match the API. Check your metrics instrument creation for obsolete parameters or missing units.
- If you have custom libraries, update their APIs to propagate units correctly.

---

## **Relevant PRs and Docs**
- [OpenTelemetry-Go release v1.16.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.16.0)
- [Metric API migration notes](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/4271)
- [OpenTelemetry Specification unit clarification](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/3248)

---

## **Summary Table**

| Old Style              | New Style (v1.16.0+)                  |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| meter.Int64Counter("x")| meter.Int64Counter("x", metric.WithUnit("unit")) |

---

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"In **OpenTelemetry Go** (as of v1.16.0), metrics are handled using the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric` package. The older metric instruments like `Int64Counter` have gone through some changes, and the API may look a bit different from earlier versions.

If you want to **create an int64 counter metric with a specific unit** in OpenTelemetry Go v1.16.0, you would do it as follows:

### Example: Creating an Int64 Counter with a Unit

#### 1. Import Required Packages

```go
import (
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric"
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/instrument"
    "context"
)
```

#### 2. Get a Meter

```go
meter := metric.NewNoopMeterProvider().Meter("example")
```
(In your real app, you should use a real meter provider.)

#### 3. Create the Counter Instrument with a Unit

```go
counter, err := meter.Int64Counter(
    "my_counter",
    instrument.WithUnit("requests"),
)
if err != nil {
    // handle error
}
```

**Key details:**
- `meter.Int64Counter` is how you declare the instrument.
- `instrument.WithUnit("requests")` will set the unit for this counter metric. Replace `"requests"` with whatever unit fits your use case (e.g., `"bytes"`, `"seconds"`, etc.).

#### 4. Use the Counter

```go
counter.Add(context.Background(), 1)
```

---

### Summary

- `WithUnit` is used as an option when creating the metric instrument.
- In v1.16.0+, instrument creation looks like:  
  ```go
  meter.Int64Counter("name", instrument.WithUnit("unit"))
  ```
- The older pattern:
  ```go
  meter.NewInt64Counter(
      "name",
      metric.WithUnit("unit"),
  )
  ```
  has been **replaced**.

Let me know if you want an example with a real exporter, or if you want to see this with the manual `metric.WithUnit` signature!","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"As of **OpenTelemetry Go v1.16.0**, the `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric` package underwent significant changes due to the metrics API stabilization. The old style instruments such as `Int64Counter` (where the type name directly encodes the value type) have been replaced with a new API.

### In v1.16.0 and newer:
- **Instrument creation** is done using the `Meter` interface and the general `Counter` interface, no longer with types like `Int64Counter`.
- Value types (e.g., int64, float64) are inferred from the method you use to record the data.

#### Example of creating and using a Counter in v1.16.0+
```go
import (
    "context"
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric"
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
)

func main() {
    meter := otel.Meter("my-meter")
    counter, err := meter.Int64Counter("my_counter")
    if err != nil {
        // handle error
    }

    ctx := context.Background()
    counter.Add(ctx, 1, attribute.String("key", "value"))
}
```

- With v1.16.0, metrics are typically created like this:
    - `Int64Counter` is constructed via `meter.Int64Counter("name")`.
    - The returned value is of type `Int64Counter`.

### Documentation
- [OpenTelemetry Go Metrics API](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/otel@v1.16.0/metric)
- [API Changes and Migration Guide](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v1160-2023-10-23)

### Summary Table

| Version | Counter Type          | Example Creation Syntax               |
|---------|----------------------|---------------------------------------|
| <1.0.0  | Int64Counter         | meter.NewInt64Counter("my_counter")   |
| >=1.16.0| Int64Counter (method)| meter.Int64Counter("my_counter")      |

If you need more help or code examples for the new API, let me know your use case!","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}

```
does not contain package go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit
```

typically means your Go code (or one of your dependencies) is trying to import the package `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit`, but that package **does not exist** in the version of the OpenTelemetry library you're using (or it's been moved or removed).

### Common Causes

1. **Version Mismatch:**  
   In recent versions of the OpenTelemetry Go library, some packages have been reorganized. The package `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit` (and sometimes even the whole `metric` API) was removed or refactored in v1.0.0 GA (around early 2024), and the API changed substantially.

2. **Stale Documentation/Tutorials:**  
   You might be following documentation or code meant for a different version of OpenTelemetry.

---

## How To Fix

### 1. **Check Your Module Version**

Run:

```bash
go list -m all | grep opentelemetry
```

Or in your `go.mod`, check which version of `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` you're using.

### 2. **Upgrade/Downgrade OpenTelemetry**

#### **If you want to use `unit`:**

- You need to **use an older version** (before v1.17.0, usually pre-2024), e.g.:

  ```bash
  go get go.opentelemetry.io/otel@v1.16.0
  ```

#### **If you're using the latest OpenTelemetry:**

- **Change your code:**  
  The `metric/unit` package is removed, and units are now usually just string constants.  
  Replace:

  ```go
  import "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit"
  ...
  unit.Milliseconds
  ```

  with
  
  ```go
  "milliseconds"
  ```

  or whatever string is needed.

---

## Example Update

**Old (before 2024):**
```go
import "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit"

meter.Float64Histogram(
    "http.server.duration",
    metric.WithUnit(unit.Milliseconds),
)
```

**New (2024+, latest API):**
```go
meter.Float64Histogram(
    "http.server.duration",
    metric.WithUnit("milliseconds"),
)
```

---

### Reference

- [OpenTelemetry Go Changelog](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Migration guides on opentelemetry-go GitHub](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go)

### Purpose

The `unit` package in OpenTelemetry Go provides standard units of measurement for metrics. These units help qualify what is being measured (e.g., bytes, milliseconds, requests) and provide a consistent way to annotate metric values with what they represent.

```go
import (

)
```

- **Module:** `opentelemetry-go`

---

### Purpose

The `unit` package in OpenTelemetry Go provides standard units of measurement for metrics. These units help qualify what is being measured (e.g., bytes, milliseconds, requests) and provide a consistent way to annotate metric values with what they represent.

---

### Typical Usage Example

```go
import (
    "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/unit"
)

meter := global.Meter("example")
metric, err := meter.Int64Counter(
    "request_count",
    metric.WithDescription("Counts number of requests"),
    metric.WithUnit(unit.Dimensionless),
)
```

Available standard units include:
- `unit.Bytes`
- `unit.Milliseconds`
- `unit.Seconds`
- `unit.Dimensionless`
- And others...

```go
var reader = metric.NewManualReader()

// ... record some measurements ...
out, _ := reader.Collect(context.Background())
```

```go
import (
```

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"This error message:

```
cannot use generic type metricdata.Histogram without instantiation
```

typically occurs in **Go** when you are trying to use a generic type without providing its required type parameter.

### Understanding the Problem

In Go 1.18 and later, you can define generic types using type parameters (e.g., `[T any]`). When you **use** such a type, you *must* specify which type you want for the parameter.

#### Example

Suppose this is the generic type definition:

```go
package metricdata

type Histogram[T any] struct {
    // fields...
}
```

If you try to do:

```go
var h metricdata.Histogram
```

You get this error, because you didn't specify a type for `T`.

### Solution

**Instantiate the generic type by specifying the type parameter.**  
For example, if you want your histogram to be of `float64` values:

```go
var h metricdata.Histogram[float64]
```

You can use any type that's allowed by the generic definition.

### Summary

- You **must** specify a type inside the square brackets for generic types.
- Example: `metricdata.Histogram[int]`, `metricdata.Histogram[float64]`, etc.

If you need help choosing the type parameter or have a code snippet you'd like to fix, please share it for a more specific solution!","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}

25. // ResourceMetrics is a collection of ScopeMetrics and the associated Resource
26. // that created them.
27. type ResourceMetrics struct {
28. 	// Resource represents the entity that collected the metrics.
29. 	Resource *resource.Resource
30. 	// ScopeMetrics are the collection of metrics with unique Scopes.
31. 	ScopeMetrics []ScopeMetrics
32. }
33. 
34. // ScopeMetrics is a collection of Metrics Produces by a Meter.
35. type ScopeMetrics struct {
36. 	// Scope is the Scope that the Meter was created with.
37. 	Scope instrumentation.Scope
38. 	// Metrics are a list of aggregations created by the Meter.
39. 	Metrics []Metrics
40. }
41. 
42. // Metrics is a collection of one or more aggregated timeseries from an Instrument.
43. type Metrics struct {
44. 	// Name is the name of the Instrument that created this data.
45. 	Name string
46. 	// Description is the description of the Instrument, which can be used in documentation.
47. 	Description string
48. 	// Unit is the unit in which the Instrument reports.
49. 	Unit string
50. 	// Data is the aggregated data from an Instrument.
51. 	Data Aggregation
52. }
53. 
54. // Aggregation is the store of data reported by an Instrument.
55. // It will be one of: Gauge, Sum, Histogram.
56. type Aggregation interface {
57. 	privateAggregation()
58. }
59. 
60. // Gauge represents a measurement of the current value of an instrument.
61. type Gauge[N int64 | float64] struct {
62. 	// DataPoints are the individual aggregated measurements with unique
63. 	// Attributes.
64. 	DataPoints []DataPoint[N]
65. }
66. 
67. func (Gauge[N]) privateAggregation() {}
68. 
69. // Sum represents the sum of all measurements of values from an instrument.
70. type Sum[N int64 | float64] struct {
71. 	// DataPoints are the individual aggregated measurements with unique
72. 	// Attributes.
73. 	DataPoints []DataPoint[N]
74. 	// Temporality describes if the aggregation is reported as the change from the
75. 	// last report time, or the cumulative changes since a fixed start time.
76. 	Temporality Temporality
77. 	// IsMonotonic represents if this aggregation only increases or decreases.
78. 	IsMonotonic bool
79. }
80. 
81. func (Sum[N]) privateAggregation() {}
82. 
83. // DataPoint is a single data point in a timeseries.
84. type DataPoint[N int64 | float64] struct {
85. 	// Attributes is the set of key value pairs that uniquely identify the
86. 	// timeseries.
87. 	Attributes attribute.Set
88. 	// StartTime is when the timeseries was started. (optional)
89. 	StartTime time.Time `json:",omitempty"`
90. 	// Time is the time when the timeseries was recorded. (optional)
91. 	Time time.Time `json:",omitempty"`
92. 	// Value is the value of this data point.
93. 	Value N
94. 
95. 	// Exemplars is the sampled Exemplars collected during the timeseries.
96. 	Exemplars []Exemplar[N] `json:",omitempty"`
97. }
98. 
99. // Histogram represents the histogram of all measurements of values from an instrument.
100. type Histogram[N int64 | float64] struct {
101. 	// DataPoints are the individual aggregated measurements with unique
102. 	// Attributes.
103. 	DataPoints []HistogramDataPoint[N]
104. 	// Temporality describes if the aggregation is reported as the change from the
105. 	// last report time, or the cumulative changes since a fixed start time.
106. 	Temporality Temporality
107. }
108. 
109. func (Histogram[N]) privateAggregation() {}
110. 
111. // HistogramDataPoint is a single histogram data point in a timeseries.
112. type HistogramDataPoint[N int64 | float64] struct {
113. 	// Attributes is the set of key value pairs that uniquely identify the
114. 	// timeseries.
115. 	Attributes attribute.Set
116. 	// StartTime is when the timeseries was started.
117. 	StartTime time.Time
118. 	// Time is the time when the timeseries was recorded.
119. 	Time time.Time
120. 
121. 	// Count is the number of updates this histogram has been calculated with.
122. 	Count uint64
123. 	// Bounds are the upper bounds of the buckets of the histogram. Because the
124. 	// last boundary is +infinity this one is implied.
125. 	Bounds []float64
126. 	// BucketCounts is the count of each of the buckets.
127. 	BucketCounts []uint64
128. 
129. 	// Min is the minimum value recorded. (optional)
130. 	Min Extrema[N]
131. 	// Max is the maximum value recorded. (optional)
132. 	Max Extrema[N]
133. 	// Sum is the sum of the values recorded.
134. 	Sum N
135. 
136. 	// Exemplars is the sampled Exemplars collected during the timeseries.
137. 	Exemplars []Exemplar[N] `json:",omitempty"`
138. }
139. 
140. // Extrema is the minimum or maximum value of a dataset.
141. type Extrema[N int64 | float64] struct {
142. 	value N
143. 	valid bool
144. }
145. 
146. // NewExtrema returns an Extrema set to v.
147. func NewExtrema[N int64 | float64](v N) Extrema[N] {
148. 	return Extrema[N]{value: v, valid: true}
149. }
150. 
151. // Value returns the Extrema value and true if the Extrema is defined.
152. // Otherwise, if the Extrema is its zero-value, defined will be false.
153. func (e Extrema[N]) Value() (v N, defined bool) {
154. 	return e.value, e.valid
155. }
156. 
157. // Exemplar is a measurement sampled from a timeseries providing a typical
158. // example.
159. type Exemplar[N int64 | float64] struct {
160. 	// FilteredAttributes are the attributes recorded with the measurement but
161. 	// filtered out of the timeseries' aggregated data.
162. 	FilteredAttributes []attribute.KeyValue
163. 	// Time is the time when the measurement was recorded.
164. 	Time time.Time
165. 	// Value is the measured value.
166. 	Value N
167. 	// SpanID is the ID of the span that was active during the measurement. If
168. 	// no span was active or the span was not sampled this will be empty.
169. 	SpanID []byte `json:",omitempty"`
170. 	// TraceID is the ID of the trace the active span belonged to during the
171. 	// measurement. If no span was active or the span was not sampled this will
172. 	// be empty.
173. 	TraceID []byte `json:",omitempty"`
